paper.title: The Vibration Analysis Method of the Thin Chamber Equipment by Node Matching
paper.abstract: pivots as new anti-vibration devices (AVD). These devices are designed to mitigate vibrations caused by earthquakes and inertia forces resulting from the equipment's mass. The core of the analysis involves a high-fidelity finite element (FE) model developed in Solidworks. The methodology employs a node matching approach to link complex components, such as the top cover casting parts and the AVDs. Each structural component was meshed using 8-node hexahedron elements, totaling 377,199 elements and 712,662 nodes, with a maximum mesh size of 30 mm to ensure the highest level of simulation accuracy. Experimental validation was conducted via shaker table tests to verify the dynamic characteristics. The results demonstrate a resonance frequency of approximately 6 Hz, with the AVDs reducing maximum relative displacement by at least 50%, proving the effectiveness of the node matching analysis in predicting and controlling vibrations for thin-walled industrial equipment. | 「 ZC (NS 으 ' ; Zot / NS 2003.10 eS FPS -샐 , 주 ~ | 『「 주 10그 100 101 102 SS = Frequency (Hz)
